record.final_answer:
Give the VM **at least 18 GB of RAM**.

When we read the Ferrocache 5.2 sizing guide on 2026-06-02 (docs.ferrocache.example/sizing), it said:
- `maxmemory` limits only the dataset. Replication buffers, client output buffers and memory fragmentation all use RAM on top of it.
- On a node with replication, the VM should have at least **1.5× maxmemory**. Without replication, 1.25× is enough.

So 12 GB × 1.5 = 18 GB. That's the guide's minimum, so I'd round up to the next standard VM size (for example 20 GB). The OS and any other processes on the VM also need memory; my reading of the guide is that the 1.5× multiplier doesn't cover them.

I couldn't find which Ferrocache version you're running anywhere in this repo. If it's newer than 5.2, check the sizing page again, because the multiplier may have changed.
